items.title: Russian military channels are increasingly painting a pretty clear picture around Lyman: the situation is getting harder for Russian forces. From what we can piece together, Russian units have been pushed back toward the Zherebets River (we still need visual confirmation of some towns), which now appears to be the main defensive line across much of this sector. But Ukraine has not stopped at the river. Russian sources themselves acknowledge crossings at several points, with Ukrainian troops pushing toward Terny and Balka Zhuravky and operating around Novosadove. Further south, fighting is reported around Zarichne while Russian channels also mention continued Ukrainian assault-group activity in and around Lyman. What stands out most in the Russian reporting is the strain on their own forces. Units are described as badly depleted, while Ukrainian formations are portrayed as fresher and reinforced. At the same time, Ukrainian strikes on crossings over the Zherebets and heavy drone activity are making resupply increasingly difficult. Some Russian accounts even claim ammunition is being carried forward on foot over long distances. Our assessment is fairly straightforward: this is not (yet) a collapse of the Russian front around Lyman, but it is sustained and increasing pressure, and the trend is clearly unfavorable for Russia. The most important point is that the Zherebets is no longer just the line Russian forces fell back to. Ukrainian troops are already getting across it in places and trying to build on those gains further east.

items.title: "Russia’s oil-processing is being degraded as sanctions prevent the refining industry from recovering from more intense and precise Ukrainian drone strikes, according to the International Energy Agency. 'It now appears likely that the persistent drone strikes and the patchwork nature of repairs are having a cumulative negative effect and degrading the refining system,' the Paris-based agency said in a monthly oil report published Friday. In August, the Russian oil refineries were hit at least 22 times, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, according to a Bloomberg tally based on public statements from both nations. The IEA revised down its baseline outlook for Russian oil processing over the next 18 months to around 4 million barrels a day, down 30% from levels before the invasion of Ukraine, it said." https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-11/ukraine-strikes-degrade-russian-oil-refining-industry-iea-says

Alexander De Croo, head of the UN development agency, said there was a risk of ‘humanitarian catastrophe’ if Russian attacks cut off access to power and water.
Speaking in Ukraine, De Croo – the UN's third most senior official – accused Russia of systematically targeting the country's energy infrastructure. He said there was now a ‘race against the clock’ to repair the power network before winter sets in and temperatures plummet.”

This is the 1st instance in months of a Russian military ship being docked there, month after the announcement that Russia’s bases in Syria would be 'transferred' to Damascus.
items.summary:
1/ EXCLUSIVE: at @RFERL we obtained photos of a Russian flotilla in Tartus port, taken early September. This is the 1st instance in months of a Russian military ship being docked there, month after the announcement that Russia’s bases in Syria would be 'transferred' to Damascus.
GeoInsider (@InsiderGeo)
UPDATE: 🇷🇺🇸🇾 After around two months of absence, Russia is back in the Mediterranean, with a Russian naval convoy now arriving at Tartus, Syria.
Our team at @SONARROW_OSINT has been tracking the convoy since August 25. The four Russian vessels have travelled from the Atlantic into the Mediterranean and across the region before reaching the Syrian coast.
The SPARTA Ro-Ro cargo ship and AKADEMIK PASHIN replenishment oiler are now docked at Tartus. The SPARTA appears to have already unloaded its cargo.
The ADMIRAL LEVCHENKO Udaloy-class destroyer and GENERAL SKOBELEV tanker are not currently inside the port. They may be operating offshore, similar to how the ADMIRAL FLOTA KASATONOV has operated around Tartus in recent months.
What exactly was delivered to Tartus remains unclear, but the return of a Russian convoy to the Syrian port after months away is significant.
So the key questions remain: What did SPARTA bring to Syria, and how long will the Russian vessels remain at Tartus?
— https://nitter.netbub.com/InsiderGeo/status/2098012800320749673#m

items.title: RT by @COUPSURE: Driving through rural Switzerland. Cows, church steeples, the whole postcard. Then a billboard: "No to war. Yes to neutrality." For a second I wasn't in Switzerland. I was in Georgia. Same slogan. In Georgia "No to war" is on the lips of every pro-Russian politician and every government official, while the war Russia started sits 40 km from the capital. Same simulated war-news videos, same "they want to drag us into war," same voice telling you the only danger is your own government. Let me spell it out: nobody is dragging Switzerland into a war. items.title: RT by @RALee85: Latest on Ukraine talks: People familiar with the talks in Kyiv tell @FT Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner brought updated versions of earlier documents, revised to reflect the changed circumstances since peace negotiations stalled in February, at the outset of the US war with Iran. But the Trump envoys came with few new ideas, the people said, and were instead seeking to revive earlier proposals and to narrow differences between Kyiv and Moscow. A central issue is the remaining Ukrainian-held territory in the Donbas, which Russia has claimed as its own but has failed to capture despite years of fighting. The eastern region, some 75% of which is under Russian control, is a red line for Zelenskyy, who has insisted that Ukraine would never hand over that territory or any other territory that Moscow’s forces occupy. https://www.ft.com/content/1e2d9db0-cb2c-4c79-942b-f0aff960e4c5?syn-25a6b1a6=1
